answers: Q1: Tiers are fraction-gated per 100-yr turn (>=8% full, 2-7.9% half), independent of absolute ops/s; one tier per line per turn is a hard pipeline cap; parallel sites do not stack. The only levers are (a) the research sink temperature, which sets the floor (floor = 2.9e-19 x T/300) but barely changes the number of steps while E >> floor, and (b) nothing else: ~25 turns to the 1e-18 J gate (~yr 3300).

Q2: Credit accrual is fraction x years, independent of ops/s. Credit is agent-wide knowledge: it may be spent at any domain you own, including a future core elsewhere (after light-delay for the order).

Q3: Research runs at the named target domain; siting does not change tier speed. Siting matters only through the sink T you can honestly declare (colder site -> lower floor) and, for a core, through the coolant-inventory rule below.

Q4: The floor floats with the sink T you declare for the line, provided you actually operate a radiator loop at that T. A 30 K loop would give floor 2.9e-20 J for research declared at that sink. But new GM rule (12): a pumped coolant loop needs inventory m_c = 2 P L /(c_p dT v) with c_p = 1e3 J/kg/K, dT = T_rad/2, v = 1 km/s (coolant-velocity research x1.26/tier, cap 10 km/s), L = sqrt(A_rad/4pi); and a radiator cannot sit below the local equilibrium T (inside your 300 K swarm that is ~300 K; a 30 K sink must be >=100s of AU outside the swarm, so L explodes). m_c scales as P^1.5 / T^3: cold loops are prohibitively heavy, hot loops cheap. Plan the core's sink T with that trade in mind.
